summary: Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers. She held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leendert A. van Daalen (1939–1993) was an Indologist. He earned an MA and PhD at Utrecht University, studying under Jan Gonda and Henk Bodewitz. He served as Lecturer of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1966–1992) and held a post at Leiden University (1992).

Lei Huang is a Tibetologist who studied at the Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2012. In 2022, Huang was appointed Assistant Professor at Capital Normal University.

Lei Rong specializes in Tibetology and education. Rong earned a BSc from East China Normal University and completed an Erasmus Mundus Masters across the University of Oslo, University of Roehampton, and Charles University (2015–2017), later holding a post at Xizang Minzu University.
Leigh Lisker (1918–2006) was a linguist and Indologist. He completed his BA at the University of Pennsylvania (ca. 1937–1941) and later served there as Assistant Professor from 1948 to 1989.

Lemuel Sadoc was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who received a PhD from Goethe University Frankfurt in 1924. Sadoc served as a professor at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, in 1926 and taught languages at the Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad.

Leo Buschardt (1906–1966) worked in Indology and religious studies, completing an MA at the University of Copenhagen (1925–1935). He held library posts at the Royal Veterinary and Agricultural University in 1943 and the Royal Danish Library as head librarian in 1944.

Leo Frobenius (1873–1938) was a historian and archaeologist. He held posts at the Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte, the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), and the Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938).

Leo Joachim Frachtenberg (1883–1930) was a linguist who studied at Cornell and Columbia universities, working under Franz Boas and A. V. Williams Jackson. He lectured at Columbia University (1910–1912) and was an ethnologist at the Bureau of American Ethnology (ca. 1912–1917).

Leo M. Pruden (1937–1991) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Taitetsu Unno. He taught at Brown University (1970–1971), Nyingma Institute (1971), and the University of Oriental Studies (attested 1988–1991).

Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Benfey, Bopp, and Grimm. He taught at the University of Göttingen (1856, 1862–1865, 1898) and held a chair at the University of Tartu (1865–1899).
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indology researcher who studied at and served as a research project staff member (Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter) at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Leo Strauss (1899–1973) was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, and Marburg, and under Ernst Cassirer. His academic appointments included Cambridge, The New School, Columbia, Chicago (ca. 1949–1969), Hebrew University, Claremont McKenna, and St. John's College.

Leo von Mankowski (1858–1909) was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Breslau, and Vienna under Georg Bühler, Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, and Alfred Hillebrandt. He held positions as Docent of Sanskrit (1894) and extraordinary professor (1904) at Jagiellonian University.

Leon Cyboran (1928–1977) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Breslau, Wroclaw University of Economics and Business, and the University of Warsaw. He taught at the University of Warsaw (1965–1973) and became a professor at KUL in 1973.

Leon Hurvitz (1923–1992) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Chicago and earned a PhD from Columbia University. He served as Assistant Professor at the University of Washington (ca. 1962–1971) and Professor at UBC (1971–1988).
Leon Sommers Swartzberg Jr. (1921–2001) was an Indologist who earned an MA at Columbia University between 1962 and 1966. In 1970, he taught anthropology at Southern Oregon University.

Leonard Bloomfield (1887–1949) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held faculty posts at Cincinnati, Illinois, Ohio State, Chicago, and served as Sterling Professor of Linguistics at Yale (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé (born 1946) is a historian and Sinologist. He studied at Leiden University between approximately 1970 and 1986, and later held a post there from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and teacher F. E. L. Priestley, and held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).
